best_for: Windows users with large NTFS drives who know part of a file name and want it on screen as they type, without waiting on Windows Search.
description:
Everything is a file search tool for Windows made by voidtools. voidtools says it collects no user data, runs fully offline and sends no telemetry, so your searches stay on your PC.

You type part of a name and the list fills in. Add *.pdf to see only PDFs, put a backslash in front of a folder name such as \downloads to look only there, or type d: to stick to one drive. A space joins two terms, a vertical bar means either one, and an exclamation mark leaves a word out. If you would rather not learn the syntax, the Advanced Search window builds the query for you. Bookmarks and search history let you rerun the searches you use most.

points.title: Names, not contents
points.text: Everything indexes file and folder names only, so the first index takes seconds: about 5 seconds for 250,000 files and about a minute for a million. A `content:` search can look inside files, but contents are not indexed, so that kind of search is slow.

points.title: NTFS gets live updates
points.text: NTFS volumes are indexed on their own and kept current through the NTFS change journal. FAT, FAT32, exFAT, mapped drives and network shares have to be added by hand as folder indexes. The FAQ lists Windows XP through Windows 11.

points.title: Light on memory
points.text: The FAQ puts it at about 35 MB of RAM for 250,000 files and about 100 MB for a million. Version 1.4 stores sizes and dates by default for faster sorting, which uses more memory; you can turn that off.

points.title: Free, with no ads
points.text: voidtools gives it away and asks for donations. The FAQ states it carries no adware or spyware, and the bundled license text is MIT.

points.title: Admin once, or the service
points.text: Reading NTFS indexes needs either the Everything service or running as administrator. Installing the service lets you run it as a normal user without a UAC prompt each time.

points.title: Many builds to choose from
points.text: There are .exe and MSI installers for x86 and x64, plus portable ZIPs that also come in ARM and Arm64. A Lite edition drops the built-in FTP and HTTP servers and the command-line and SDK hooks. The `es` command-line tool is a separate download.

points.title: 1.5 is still beta
points.text: The 1.5 line is offered as a 64-bit beta next to the stable 1.4.1 release. This site keeps 11 Windows versions of the stable line.
